::: {#exr-racket-assoc}
#### Looking up a vertex

In Racket, the adjacency list of the office graph (@exm-adjacency-list) can be stored as a list with one list for each vertex,
which starts with the vertex and goes on with its neighbors:

```racket
(define office
  '((a b c)
    (b a c d)
    (c a b e)
    (d b e f)
    (e c d f)
    (f d e)))
```

The quote `'` makes Racket read what follows as data, so `'(a b c)` is the same list as `(list 'a 'b 'c)`.
`(assoc x L)` returns the first element of the list `L` whose first element is `x`, and `#f` if there is none.
What does `(assoc 'd office)` return?

:::
